instruction: Guide me on how to make my terminal's 10000-line scrollback setting remain after reboot.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.write('gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$(gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default | tr -d "'"')/ scrollback-lines'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to persistently set terminal scrollback to 10000 lines. The evaluator opens a new terminal and checks the scrollback-lines setting using gsettings command. Expected output should contain '10000' indicating scrollback is configured correctly. Similar pattern to original task (checking terminal configuration persistence).
metadata.verification: Verified that gsettings command will return '10000' when scrollback-lines is set to 10000. The postconfig executes gsettings to retrieve the scrollback configuration from the default terminal profile.
